clue.text: See 20
Maybe Hollande's foe had to reform, say

indicators.note: to reform is to reshape, so the letters of the two words before are rebuilt into a new order

parts.note: to say is to state, declare

explanation.surface: François Hollande's political opponent had to change his ways, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to reform' rearranges FOE HAD into HEADOF. 'Maybe' marks Hollande, the former French president, as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: François Hollande, as President of France, was an example of a national leader holding the top constitutional office.

clue.text: Musical boy tucking into extremely mouldy brownie

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes, the first and last letters, of mouldy
tucking into means the boy is pushed inside the brownie

parts.note: a brownie is a household sprite, a kind of fairy
a boy is a lad

explanation.surface: A lad is eating a rather mouldy chocolate cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brownie' reads as the chocolate cake, but here it is the helpful household sprite of folklore.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lerner and Loewe show based on Shaw's Pygmalion is a famous stage and screen musical.

clue.text: Support wages getting cut? Damn terrible vice

parts.note: to support a motion is to second it

indicators.note: getting cut means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: wages are a person's income

indicators.note: terrible signals that the letters of Damn are put into a jumbled order

explanation.surface: Someone complains that their pay is being reduced and curses an awful habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vice' looks like a wicked habit after 'terrible', but it is the prefix meaning deputy, as in vice-captain.
explanation.definitionFit: A vice-president or vice-captain is the deputy, the officer ranking just below the leader.

clue.text: Destroying Gulf, even seeking to do harm

indicators.note: destroying something breaks it apart, so the letters of the next two words are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: Wrecking the Gulf region, even out of a desire to cause damage.
explanation.definitionFit: A vengeful person wants revenge, so is bent on hurting whoever wronged them.

clue.text: Many countries like raising capital

parts.note: like, as in 'such as', means as

indicators.note: in a down clue raising lifts the word so it reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: capital as slang for excellent is A1, written here as the letters A and I

explanation.surface: Several nations behave like one another when raising money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like money or a chief city; it is the old exclamation of approval, equal to A1.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest continent contains dozens of nations, so it fairly stands for many countries.

clue.text: Lane found in court by queen's secluded area

indicators.note: found in tells us the Lane is located inside the court abbreviation

parts.note: Lois Lane is the reporter in the Superman stories
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the queen

explanation.surface: A narrow road runs into a courtyard beside the queen's private garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lane' reads as a small road but is Lois Lane, Superman's colleague at the Daily Planet.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloister is a covered walk round a quiet courtyard in a monastery, a place withdrawn from the world.

clue.text: What Molly Bloom said about snatching kiss is erotic

indicators.note: snatching means grabbing something and holding it inside
about turns the word round so it reads backwards

parts.note: Molly Bloom's soliloquy closing Joyce's Ulysses ends on the word yes
X stands for a kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: Joyce's heroine's famous final word, taking in a kiss, is sensual.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sexually exciting or arousing is erotic in the everyday sense.

clue.text: Gas from wicked, heartless Tory, poor in speech

parts.note: wicked and ace are both slang for excellent

indicators.note: heartless removes the inside letters, leaving the two ends of Tory
in speech means the following word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: poor in the sense of thin or meagre means lean

explanation.surface: Hot air comes from a nasty Conservative who is a weak speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wicked' reads as evil, but in slang it means great, like ACE.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetylene is a flammable hydrocarbon gas used in welding torches.

clue.text: What you need to do here is 2 28, 4 24 across, 14 27, 23 12 and 20 1

definitions.text: What you need to do here

parts.note: the linked entry at 2 and 28 read as an instruction gives the opening letter of the word in entry 28
read as an instruction this pair asks for the second letter of the word at 24 across
read as an instruction this pair asks for the opening letter of the word at 27
read as an instruction this pair asks for the middle letter of the word at 12
read as an instruction this pair asks for the last letter of a female horse, the word at 20 being its possessive

explanation.surface: A puzzle instruction listing the five long themed answers.
explanation.walkthrough: Each linked answer is itself a letter-picking instruction applied to its own last word: the head of one, the second of the next, and so on, spelling out the task.
explanation.definitionFit: The job of anyone tackling a crossword is to work out its answers.

clue.text: Poem mostly about a girl

indicators.note: about turns the shortened word round to read backwards
mostly means all but the last letter is used

parts.note: an idyll is a short pastoral poem

explanation.surface: A verse composition that largely concerns a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Lydia is a girl's name, borne for instance by the youngest Bennet sister in Pride and Prejudice.

clue.text: See 23
Made tender love very loudly, flushed after ecstasy

indicators.note: after places the colour word behind the drug's letter

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scores, the letter O
FF, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
flushed means red in the face

explanation.surface: Made love noisily and came over red-faced after taking a drug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tender' is the verb, as in a bid tendered, not the adjective of a loving encounter.
explanation.definitionFit: To offer something is to put it forward, which is what tendering means in business.

clue.text: Concerned with seeing old photo, taking time

indicators.note: taking means the photo word holds the time letter inside it

parts.note: a pic is a photo

explanation.surface: Interested in viewing an old snapshot that took a while.
explanation.definitionFit: Optic is the adjective relating to the eye and vision.

clue.text: Duck eggs returned in sack, about to be served?

indicators.note: in says the reversed pair goes inside the word for sack

parts.note: to sack someone is to fire them

indicators.note: returned sends both words back, reading the pair from end to start

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, nil
nits are the eggs of lice

explanation.surface: Someone stuffs bird's eggs into a bag just before the meal is dished up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' is not a bird but the cricket score of nothing; 'returned' turns both words round together, giving STINLIN, which 'in' places inside the word for sack.
explanation.definitionFit: Whoever stands at the front of a queue will be dealt with next.

clue.text: Seaman admits hesitation in philosophical activity

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so the sailor's word takes the next pieces inside

parts.note: a rating is a non-officer sailor
um is the sound of hesitation
in is taken as written

explanation.surface: A sailor confesses to uncertainty about deep thought.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruminating is pondering deeply, the kind of reflective thinking philosophers do.

clue.text: English child brought up close to Dorothy Parker may be so

indicators.note: in a down clue brought up raises the pair so they read upwards

parts.note: a son is a child

indicators.note: close to means the final letter of Dorothy

explanation.surface: An English youngster raised near the famous American wit Dorothy Parker.
explanation.walkthrough: Dorothy Parker the writer is a decoy; the definition is the phrase nosey parker, a busybody.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosey parker is an inquisitive busybody, so a Parker of that kind is prying.

clue.text: Soldiers here showing character

parts.note: British part-time soldiers are found in the Territorial Army, a British reserve force
TA is the Territorial Army, the British volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: Troops in this place display strength of personality.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Soldiers here' as 'where soldiers are': in the TA, the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet, and a letter is a character.

clue.text: Travelling troupe with car leaving piano player in Brussels

indicators.note: travelling suggests movement, so the letters are moved into a new order
leaving means the piano letter departs from the troupe

parts.note: p is the musical marking for piano, quietly

explanation.surface: A touring theatre company sets off by car, leaving behind its pianist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'player' suggests a musician, but it is someone playing a part in the EU institutions based in Brussels.
explanation.definitionFit: A Eurocrat is an official of the European Union, a figure in its Brussels headquarters.

clue.text: Bit of scale from tailless fish

indicators.note: tailless means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: the sole is a flatfish

explanation.surface: A scrap of scale comes from a fish without a tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scale' suggests the fish's skin, but it is the musical scale: doh, ray, me, fah and so on.
explanation.definitionFit: In sol-fa the fifth note of the major scale is sol (or soh).

clue.text: Get brown paper bag with no good article

parts.note: the Sun is a British tabloid newspaper

indicators.note: with no means a letter is dropped from the bag word

parts.note: taken as written
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Fetch a brown paper bag that has no decent item in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brown paper bag' reads as one object; 'Get brown' is the definition and 'paper' is the Sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying in the sunshine is how people acquire a tan.

clue.text: God of war has time to don armour in bit of cloud

indicators.note: to don is to put on, so the armour goes around the god and time

parts.note: mail is chain armour
Ares is the Greek god of war

explanation.surface: The war god pauses to put on his armour beside a wisp in the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: A mare's tail is a long wispy streak of cirrus cloud.

clue.text: Redknapp, involved in scam, makes fuss

indicators.note: involved in means the name goes inside the swindle word

parts.note: a con is a scam
Harry Redknapp, the English football manager, is known in Cockney fashion as 'Arry, dropping the H

explanation.surface: A football manager caught up in a swindle causes a stir.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry Redknapp is an English football manager; Cockney speech drops the H, leaving ARRY.
explanation.definitionFit: A carry-on is a British colloquial term for a commotion or fuss.

clue.text: Screw going round prison in fear

indicators.note: going round means the wages word surrounds the prison word

parts.note: screw is old slang for wages, pay
nick is British slang for prison or police station

explanation.surface: A prison warder doing the rounds of the jail is frightened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screw' looks like a prison warder, fitting the prison theme, but here it is slang for wages.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in a state of fear or alarm is panicky.

clue.text: Games on a particular day could be footy

indicators.note: on in a down clue puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school games
a date is a particular day

explanation.surface: Football matches happen on a set day, which might be footy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'footy' is not football but 'like a foot'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedate is a botanical term meaning shaped like a foot, so it describes something foot-like.

clue.text: Criminal forgery in VAT etc? Force must act here!

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A fraud involving sales tax: the police must intervene!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Force' looks like the police force, but it is gravitational force acting at a body's balance point.
explanation.definitionFit: Gravity acts on a body as if all its weight were concentrated at one point, its balance point.

clue.text: See 4
November 1st's around this month

indicators.note: around means the ordinal wraps around the month letter

parts.note: 1st is written as the figure one, read as I, plus ST
N is November in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: The first of November is near this month.
explanation.walkthrough: INST was formerly used in business letters to mean 'of this month'.
explanation.definitionFit: Abbreviated instant, it was used in commercial letters to refer to the current month.

clue.text: William gave Kate rank, ultimately they will inherit!

indicators.note: ultimately means the final letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: Prince William gave Kate a royal title; in the end they will inherit.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition refers to the Beatitudes: the meek shall inherit the earth.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sermon on the Mount says the humble and gentle shall inherit the earth.

clue.text: Mandarin is thus found in Washington? Almost

indicators.note: found in means the letters sit inside the following words

explanation.surface: Is the official Chinese language more or less spoken in the US capital?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mandarin' could be a bureaucrat or a fruit; it is the Chinese language, whose word meanings change with pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandarin uses pitch contours to distinguish words, which is what makes a language tonal.

clue.text: See 14
See 2
Instructions to batsman, causing some sort of accident

definitions.meaning: a batsman told to strike the ball and then dash for a single
a road collision where the driver leaves the scene

explanation.surface: Telling a cricketer what to do brings about a crash.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket call to strike and dash for a single, and a road collision whose driver flees the scene.
